text:
kevin: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a cost-attribution view: token-level costs + cache savings, broken down per-route and per-model. Want to discuss rollout into the console.

sana: Nice. Do you mean per-request raw events or pre-aggregated rollups for the UI?

kevin: Both. UI should default to daily rollups for performance, with a drilldown that shows raw events for audits. Main friction: how we attribute KV/prefix cache savings when a cached prefix serves multiple routes.

oliver: Attribution is tricky. We currently log cache hits with request_id and route_id, so technically we can attribute savings to the most recent active route, but that skews shared-cache scenarios.

anna: Could we show a "shared savings" bucket and then an attribution model (pro-rata by token or by request)? Let users pick.

matt: Pro-rata by token seems simplest and defensible. But hits for streaming responses complicate token accounting. Also need to consider model quantization tiers — cost-per-token differs.

kevin: Agreed. Plan: store raw events with fields {request_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit, cache_saved_tokens}. Rollups compute: total_tokens, billable_tokens = total_tokens - cache_saved_tokens, cost = sum(billable_tokens * model_rate). Drilldown can re-run attribution on raw events.

oliver: Storing raw per-request events at scale will blow up storage. We need retention and sampling policies. Can we sample 1% and keep full rollups for 90 days?

kevin: Yes, retention/sampling will be config per-customer. The UI should show when a view is sampled.

billing-bot: Note: current billing exports only include billable_token totals per-tenant per-day. No per-route breakdown.

anna: That's a problem for teams wanting per-feature cost centers. We should add an export that includes route_id and model_variant in daily invoices (optional flag).

matt: Another gotcha: routing policies that fallback to cheaper models will change apparent unit economics. Need to surface "effective model" used for billing, not just requested model.

kevin: Good call. We'll add fields: requested_model and served_model in both raw events and rollups. Rollup cost should use served_model.rate. UI must show a small badge when served_model != requested_model.

oliver: Query performance: current console runs a single SQL over the rollup table. If we add per-route breakdowns and multi-dim rollups (route + model + day), cardinality explodes. Consider precomputed cubes for top 100 routes, and on-demand compute for others.

kevin: Let's implement heavy-hitter precomputation + on-demand. UX: top routes visible immediately, others behind a "Compute breakdown" button that kicks off a job.

sana: For quotas: if customers set route-level quotas, cost dashboard should reflect quota hits and "savings from throttling" (i.e., prevented tokens). We track throttled_tokens in telemetry.

kevin: Add throttled_tokens to raw events and rollups. Also show a "what-if" toggle that simulates cost without throttling.

anna: API side debate: expose a new internal endpoint /v1/telemetry/costs?date=YYYY-MM-DD&group_by=route,model that returns rollups. Or just extend existing /v1/metrics to accept cost metrics. Thoughts?

matt: Prefer a new endpoint for cost to keep separation and rate limits. Cost queries can be heavy. Also add a header X-Query-Sampling to indicate sampling fraction.

oliver: We'll need auth scopes. cost:read for billing teams, cost:admin for exports.

kevin: Example query shape for the endpoint:

```
GET /v1/telemetry/costs?start=2026-03-01&end=2026-03-07&group_by=route,model&granularity=day
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Query-Sampling: 0.01
```

Response should include metadata: sampled: true/false, sampling_rate, served_model_fallback_policy.

sana: UX thing: show p50/p95 cost per-request along with average. People want tail insight.

kevin: Add percentile columns to rollups (p50_tokens, p95_tokens). We'll compute percentiles from sampled raw events.

anna: Security: for Private deployments, ensure customers can opt out of raw event export to hosted analytics. We'll provide an on-prem collector that writes rollups to local storage.

matt: Operational: alerting when cost attribution jobs lag > 30m. Currently we have a lag metric for rollups, reuse that.

oliver: Edge-case: when routing sends multi-model partial responses (ensemble), cost attribution needs to split by component model. Mark as future work.

kevin: Notes captured. Next steps: I’ll prototype UI mockups + sample API contract. @sana can you own retention/sampling UX copy? @oliver plz sketch precompute candidates and cost of cube. @matt verify auth scopes and billing export fields. @anna check private-deploy constraints.

sana: On it.

oliver: I'll run numbers on storage and query cost tomorrow.

matt: I'll draft the open api spec for the new endpoint.

anna: I'll write the security opt-out doc.

kevin: Thanks all :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Reaction added :eyes:
